html:
A volcanic eruption in southern Iceland from June 1783 to February 1784. Lava poured from a long line of craters called Laki.

The lava covered hundreds of square kilometres, and the craters released vast amounts of poisonous gas, above all sulphur and fluorine. The fluorine poisoned grass, and about half of Iceland's cattle and horses and most of its sheep died. In the famine that followed, known in Iceland as the Haze Famine, about a fifth of Iceland's people died.

The gas spread far beyond Iceland. A dry haze hung over much of Europe in the summer of 1783, and records in England and elsewhere show a rise in deaths. The winter that followed was very cold in Europe and North America. Some historians have linked the bad harvests of these years to unrest in France before the French Revolution, but that link is debated.

Laki was one of the largest lava eruptions in recorded history. A later eruption with world effects was the Tambora eruption of 1815.
sum: A volcanic eruption in southern Iceland from June 1783 to February 1784. Lava poured from a long line of craters called Laki.
